# Division of Labor {.unnumbered}

The organizing principle of this series is a clean separation: Microsoft has
built an exceptional cloud identity platform, and it solves the engine problem
precisely. What it does not — and cannot — solve is the environmental problem:
the twenty-year estate you built on a foundation it is now asking you to
replace.

Every book in the series returns to this division. This page puts it in one
place.

::: {.callout-note}
This matrix summarizes the division of labor documented in each book's
**Division of labor** callout. Read alongside the books, not instead of them —
the table names the problem; the books explain why it is a problem and how to
solve it.
:::

## The Through-Line

Reading the **What only you can provide** column top to bottom produces a
program:

1. Build the true inventory — not the Arc-discovered one, the complete one.
2. Decide what survives — retire the zombies, consolidate the stragglers,
   only then migrate what remains.
3. Measure the authentication posture of what survives — classify every
   instance, classify every NTLM finding by pattern.
4. Deploy Arc in dependency order — verify the IMDS token before declaring
   a host ready for login migration.
5. Map every AD principal to its Entra equivalent — users, groups, service
   accounts, each with a different migration path.
6. Migrate logins in parallel — create, validate, disable, observe, drop.
   Never drop before you observe.
7. Eliminate NTLM by pattern — SPN fixes first, connection-string updates
   second, domain-topology fixes last (they wait on the consolidation
   program).
8. Classify every AD group and every application in the chain — both have
   four types, each type has a different path.
9. Inventory every connection string — the last mile is also the most
   operationally intensive.
10. Verify the closure conditions continuously — the posture is not declared,
    it is measured. Phase C must arrive as a non-event.
11. Migrate the PKI before you retire ADCS — the certificate dependencies
    are invisible until they break.

Microsoft provides a platform capable of all of this.
The program is what drives the estate through it.
